identifiedPrevalence.counted: special-education students in the disability type uisasotong jangae (communication disorder)
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: special-education students in all disability types
identifiedPrevalence.note: Students recognised as special-education subjects in the disability type uisasotong jangae (communication disorder), of 95,420 in all types, 2020; Ministry of Education, 2024 Special Education Statistics, annual series by disability type. An administrative count of children the system has designated, not an epidemiological estimate; the Korean category covers communication broadly rather than language disorder alone.

identifiedPrevalence.counted: special-education students in the disability type uisasotong jangae (communication disorder)
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: special-education students in all disability types
identifiedPrevalence.note: Students recognised as special-education subjects in the disability type uisasotong jangae (communication disorder) as at 1 April 2024, 2.2% of the 115,610 in all types; Ministry of Education, 2024 Special Education Statistics. The number has moved 2,404 - 2,450 - 2,622 - 2,645 - 2,600 across 2020 to 2024 while the all-types total rose by a fifth, so the share fell from 2.5% to 2.2%. An administrative count, not an epidemiological estimate.

sources.label: Ministry of Education (Korea), 2024 Special Education Statistics (2024 teuksu gyoyuk tonggye), National Assembly Library copy

identifiedPrevalence.counted: ucenci z govorno jezikovnimi motnjami (pupils with speech and language disorders) among pupils formally directed to additional professional help
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: pupils with special needs in mainstream primary schools with adapted delivery and additional professional help
identifiedPrevalence.note: Pupils with govorno jezikovne motnje (speech and language disorders), 11.7% of the 10,091 pupils formally directed (usmerjeni) into mainstream primary schools with adapted delivery and additional professional help, 2015/16; Ministry of Education, Science and Sport, table of pupils with special needs. A count of children the placement procedure has designated, not an epidemiological estimate. It excludes pupils in adapted and special programmes.

identifiedPrevalence.counted: ucenci z govorno jezikovnimi motnjami (pupils with speech and language disorders) among pupils formally directed to additional professional help
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: pupils with special needs in mainstream primary schools with adapted delivery and additional professional help
identifiedPrevalence.note: Pupils with govorno jezikovne motnje, 13.3% of the 14,829 pupils formally directed into mainstream primary schools with adapted delivery and additional professional help, 2021/22; Ministry of Education, Science and Sport. The count rose from 1,180 in 2015/16 while the directed population rose by half, so the category's share rose from 11.7% to 13.3%. It excludes pupils in adapted and special programmes.

sources.label: Ministrstvo za izobrazevanje, znanost in sport (Slovenia), Podatki v zvezi z ucenci s posebnimi potrebami v osnovnih solah s prilagojenim izvajanjem in dodatno strokovno pomocjo

identifiedPrevalence.counted: children in the Growing Up in New Zealand cohort whose mothers expressed concern about speech at 54 months and who had received speech-language therapy to some extent
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: 776 mothers who expressed concern about their child's speech at 54 months
identifiedPrevalence.note: Of 776 mothers in the Growing Up in New Zealand cohort who expressed concern about their child's speech at 54 months, 338 (46.2%) had received speech-language therapy intervention to some extent; MSD Children and Families Research Fund, Access to Speech-language Therapy Services in Aotearoa New Zealand. This is service receipt in one birth cohort as reported by mothers, not a count of children the system identified and not an epidemiological estimate.

identifiedPrevalence.counted: children whose mothers reported concerns about communication at 54 months
identifiedPrevalence.denominator: children in the Growing Up in New Zealand cohort
identifiedPrevalence.note: Mothers reported concerns about the communication of 13% of children at 54 months, and 56% of those children had received some intervention for communication; MSD Children and Families Research Fund, Access to Speech-language Therapy Services in Aotearoa New Zealand. The figure is mother-reported concern in one birth cohort, not a clinical or administrative identification, and the report gives 16% at two years for comparison.
